language.script_notes: English-only signage throughout — the lack of Welsh or Gaelic on signs is itself a clue that separates England from Wales and Scotland.

road_furniture.line_paint: As national; double yellow lines along kerbs, white studs between dashes.
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; dense formal infrastructure in London and the cities.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national — mph signs, circular pole attachments, black-and-white striped crossing poles with yellow balls.

architecture.roof_style: Steeply pitched roofs with rows of chimney pots; thatch on rural cottages in southern and western counties.
architecture.roof_material: Clay tile, slate, and thatch; Cotswold limestone tiles in the Cotswolds.
architecture.wall_construction: Red-brick terraces and semi-detached houses dominate towns and cities; honey-coloured Cotswold limestone cottages; half-timbered Tudor buildings in the Midlands and southeast; Victorian industrial brick in the north.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Red and brown brick, warm honey stone in the Cotswolds, and whitewashed or plastered cottage walls.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Long brick terraces; thatched Cotswold and Devon cottages; Georgian townhouses; Victorian mills and viaducts in the north; village greens with a church and pub.

nature.vegetation: Hedge-bordered patchwork fields, mixed deciduous woodland (oak, beech), and heather moorland in the northern uplands.
nature.terrain: Mostly rolling lowland farmland, with chalk downs in the south, the Pennines in the north, and the Lake District and Dartmoor as upland areas.
nature.climate_signature: Mild, often overcast and drizzly, generally drier in the east than the west.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — white front, yellow rear.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: London's red double-decker buses and black taxi cabs; otherwise the standard national mix.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense, near-complete coverage including narrow rural lanes.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture and plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: England has English-only signage; Wales shows bilingual Welsh-first signs and 'ARAF' road markings, and Scotland shows Gaelic on some signs with moorland and lochs.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Left-hand traffic, English signage, double yellow lines, hedgerows
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Circular UK pole attachments versus Ireland's rectangular ones, blue versus green distance markers, 'GIVE WAY' versus 'YIELD', and mph versus km/h.
